strengths: Well-motivated problem with compelling preliminary analysis showing anti-correlation between response length and accuracy (Table 1, Figure 2)
Training-free and model-agnostic design enables practical deployment without requiring supervised fine-tuning or reinforcement learning
Consistent empirical improvements across multiple models (7B and 1.5B) and datasets, with notable reduction in repetition frequency (6.7%→1.3% for 7B on AIME2024)
Clear presentation with helpful illustrative examples (Figures 3-4) and well-structured algorithm description
Addresses a practical problem of overthinking in LRMs with real implications for inference latency and accuracy
weaknesses: Severely limited evaluation scope: only 30 problems per dataset (60 total), 2 model variants from same family, 5 random seeds insufficient for statistical significance; no significance testing despite high variance
No comparison with relevant recent baselines: O1-Pruner, AdaptThink, AutoL2S, ThinkPrune, Chain of Draft, or even simple baselines like beam search - only compared against standard inference
Arbitrary hyperparameter choices (K=3, τ=2.5) with no justification, ablation studies, or sensitivity analysis; different temperatures for different datasets unexplained
Unclear computational efficiency: no wall-clock time comparisons, memory overhead of parallel branching unanalyzed, token-length reduction does not necessarily translate to actual speedup

Technical ambiguity in Algorithm 1, line 6: uses 'max' on indicator which may select longest rather than shortest completed sequence; end-to-end approximation quality relative to oracle never quantified
High variance in results across models and datasets (8% → 2% improvement for 1.5B AIME2025) without explanation; evaluation limited to mathematical reasoning with unknown generalization

Methodological concern: oracle analysis (100 samples) doesn't establish shorter paths are universally optimal - could be confounded by problem difficulty rather than causal length-accuracy relationship

strengths: Well-motivated empirical observation of length-accuracy anti-correlation demonstrated across multiple models and datasets (Figure 2) with reasonable theoretical connection to GRPO training objectives

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 diverse LRMs and 4 reasoning datasets showing consistent and substantial improvements (14% average) in both accuracy and reduction of repetitive generation
Practical training-free and plug-and-play design enables immediate deployment on existing models without retraining
Clear presentation with helpful visualizations and concrete examples demonstrating failure cases (standard inference) and corrections (DTS)
Achieves impressive efficiency gains (Figure 5) enabling smaller models to outperform larger models under matched compute budgets
Demonstrates model agnosticism across different architectures, suggesting generalizability
weaknesses: Limited novelty: selective branching in tree search and early termination strategies are not new; the contribution is mostly applying existing ideas with a new entropy+varentropy heuristic for decision tokens, which is incremental

Theoretical justification incomplete: while GRPO analysis provides motivation, the length-accuracy correlation is observed empirically and the causality is not definitively established; other factors (more tokens = more error opportunities) could explain the pattern

Fixed hyperparameters across all tasks (τᵥ=1.5, τₕ=2.5, K=3, 48-branch limit) lack strong justification; Table 4 shows limited sensitivity analysis but universal optimality across diverse tasks is questionable

Critical ablation studies missing: no isolation of tree structure contribution vs. selection strategy contribution; unclear whether gains come from structured exploration or the early-termination heuristic
Statistical rigor lacking: no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests despite averaging over only 5 runs; high variance in improvements across tasks (1.82% to 38%) not explained
Computational overhead not thoroughly analyzed: memory requirements and latency implications of maintaining up to 48 active branches unexplored; unclear token budget equivalence with baselines
Inconsistent improvements across models and datasets: some improvements are modest (Qwen3 GPQA-D: +1.82%) while others are substantial, suggesting task-dependence not fully understood

Missing key baseline comparisons: no comparison with classical beam search, speculative decoding, or other recent tree search methods; unclear if results differ from standard beam search with equal compute budget
Case studies in Appendix B are cherry-picked success examples with no systematic analysis of failure modes or conditions where DTS underperforms
Incomplete reproducibility: decision token thresholds universality unclear, PFLOPs calculation methodology not detailed, only Huggingface models evaluated

strengths: Comprehensive empirical validation of length-accuracy anti-correlation across 4 models and 4 datasets, demonstrating consistent and reproducible observations
Strong experimental results with substantial improvements (14% average) across diverse reasoning datasets and architectures
Practical training-free method that can be applied as a plug-and-play module to existing LRMs
Addresses multiple failure modes including repetitive generation and provides quantitative metrics for improvements
Clear presentation with well-structured experiments covering multiple research questions (accuracy, repetition, trajectory quality)
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Core contribution (exploiting length-accuracy anti-correlation for early stopping) is relatively straightforward; using entropy/varentropy for branching is a standard technique application

Weak theoretical justification: GRPO-based explanation in Section 2.2 is post-hoc and circular—training-time bias should not necessarily manifest at inference time in the claimed way; lacks rigorous causal analysis

Unfair experimental comparisons: Computational cost during decoding is never clearly quantified (wall-clock time, FLOPs, memory); unclear if selective branching truly matches independent sampling budgets; Figure 5's PFLOPs comparison is imprecise

Ad-hoc design choices lack principled justification: decision token criteria (low entropy AND high varentropy) is not well-motivated; thresholds (τᵥ=1.5, τₕ=2.5) appear fixed without clear tuning procedure; 48-branch cap is arbitrary

Narrow scope and generalization concerns: Evaluation limited to math/STEM reasoning with deterministic answers; no evidence for open-ended reasoning; unexplored failure modes where longer reasoning might be necessary; anti-correlation reliability not analyzed

Missing critical analyses: No statistics on actual branching patterns; no failure mode analysis; limited hyperparameter sensitivity studies; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; absent discussion of when and why the method might fail
Potentially misleading claims: 'Small models outperform large models' comparison conflates better decoding with better reasoning; assumes anti-correlation holds universally without demonstrated proof
Reproducibility concerns: Source code URL missing; hyperparameter tuning procedure undocumented; unclear if thresholds were selected on development set

strengths: Clear empirical insight: Identifies and validates length-accuracy anti-correlation with both empirical evidence and GRPO-based theoretical justification
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 4 LRMs × 4 datasets with consistent improvements (~14% average), comprehensive metrics including repetition rate and computational efficiency
High practical utility: Training-free, inference-time method immediately applicable to existing LRMs without modification; enables small models to match flagship model performance
Solid experimental design: Appropriate baselines (Self-Consistency, DeepConf), ablation studies, statistical rigor (5 random seeds), thorough case studies demonstrating mitigation of repetition loops
Well-presented and reproducible: Clear writing with informative visualizations, implementation details in appendix, hyperparameters specified, code promised
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Entropy/varentropy-based branching and tree-based decoding are known techniques; primary contribution is their combination motivated by the length-accuracy observation, which is somewhat incremental

Theoretical justification incomplete: GRPO analysis (Eq. 1) provides intuition but lacks rigor in connecting training-time length bias to test-time anti-correlation; no formal analysis of tree sketching approximation quality

Early termination strategy suboptimal: DTS-Stable consistently outperforms DTS-Greedy (Table 1), undermining the core 'early termination' principle; voting budget B=8 appears arbitrary without justification

Hyperparameter choices lack principled justification: Fixed τᵥ=1.5, τₕ=2.5, K=3 across all models/datasets; hard branch limit of 48 is clearly ad-hoc; limited ablation studies (Table 4 only tests entropy threshold)
Incomplete computational analysis: Wall-clock time overhead not reported, only PFLOPs; memory cost of 48 parallel branches unknown; practical branch limit may constrain exploration

Generalization concerns: All datasets are mathematical reasoning tasks; all models are RL-trained reasoning models; unclear if length-accuracy anti-correlation holds for other domains, architectures, or training methods
Statistical rigor: No confidence intervals or significance tests despite small dataset sizes (30-200 questions); unclear if improvements are statistically significant
Missing important baselines: No comparison with standard beam search (natural baseline); some design choices appear arbitrary relative to established tree search methods
